summary:

title: Bangladesh's power tariff hike to hit textile-apparel sector hard
summary:

Sectors like textiles and garments that are heavily dependent on electricity may face the biggest impact. 
Listed textile-garment firms could face additional challenges in maintaining global competitiveness.

title: Forced-labour tariffs: Fashion’s next border shock
summary:
The proposed US Section 301 forced-labour tariffs could reshape apparel sourcing by making labour traceability a direct landed-cost factor. Apparel supply chains across Asia face tighter scrutiny as buyers must prove fibre, yarn and labour origins to avoid tariff and detention risks.
With the EU also tightening forced-labour rules, compliance and transparent sourcing may become important.

title: ICE cotton eases on stronger US dollar, improved rainfall outlook
summary:
ICE cotton futures eased in a narrow trading range as a stronger US dollar reduced the competitiveness of US exports and improved weather conditions boosted crop prospects.
The July 2026 contract settled at 76.73 cents per pound.
Market sentiment remained cautious as favourable US supply expectations and rising certified stocks offset support from India’s temporary cotton import duty waiver.

title: Canada wants FTA with US, Mexico to be renewed for 16 years
summary:
Canada has given the US and Mexico official notice that it wants their FTA to be renewed for 16 years when it comes up for review on July 1.
Canada’s US Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc travelled to the US to meet USTR Jamieson Greer after sending a letter to Greer and Mexico's secretary of economy Marcelo Ebrard.
Getting relief from President Donald Trump's tariffs tops Canada’s agenda for the talks.

title: Australian industry index weak in May amid rising input costs: AIG
summary:
Industrial conditions were weak in Australia in May due to the energy crisis, which is weighing heavily on new orders. 
Firms reported widespread delays in investments. 
Persistent economic uncertainty, rising unemployment and limited capital investment are expected to continue weighing on capacity utilisation in future. 
Businesses cited reduced customer spending and increased price sensitivity.

title: US-Bangladesh textile pact: Zero tariffs vs supply chain realities
summary:
A new US-Bangladesh trade agreement could allow certain Bangladeshi apparel exports to enter the US at zero tariff if they use US-origin cotton and textile inputs.
While the move may improve competitiveness and boost US cotton imports, industry experts caution that longer shipping times, higher costs, and reliance on regional supply chains could slow a shift away from current suppliers.

title: Strait of Hormuz disruptions to hit 1 bn lives in LDCs, SIDS: UNCTAD
summary:
The Strait of Hormuz disruptions are sending shockwaves through the global energy system and vulnerable economies are on the front line: of 75 such economies, 65 depend on imported oil, UNCTAD said.
For these, rising energy prices will translate into higher costs and difficult trade-offs between covering fuel bills and investing in essential public services.
This will affect nearly a billion lives.

title: Poland’s economy to grow 3.5% in 2026: EBRD
summary:

The fiscal deficit is projected at 6.8 per cent in 2026, with debt rising to 65 per cent of GDP.
However, higher energy prices, trade tensions and weak external demand prompted the bank to cut its forecasts.

title: US logistics expansion remains strong in May despite cost pressures
summary:
The US Logistics Managers’ Index eased slightly to 69.5 in May 2026 but remained near a four-year high, signalling strong sector expansion. 
Transportation prices hit a record high amid Strait of Hormuz-related fuel disruptions, while inventory and warehousing costs also surged. 
Researchers warned persistent logistics inflation could pressure supply chains and broader economic activity.

title: Sri Lanka’s garment exports fall 7.4% to $1.5 bn in Jan-April 2026

Combined textile and apparel exports totalled $1.62 billion, accounting for 45.7 per cent of industrial exports.
April textile and garment exports also weakened amid continued global demand uncertainty.

title: South Korea’s apparel imports rebound in April, reach $4.05 bn
summary:

Knitwear imports outperformed woven garments, while exports of man-made filaments and knitted fabrics declined amid weaker global demand and growing competition from lower-cost textile-producing countries.

title: The invisible tariff: Compliance is now apparel’s toughest border
summary:
Tariffs are no longer the only trade barrier, as proof of origin, traceability, labour compliance and sustainability data increasingly determine market access.
EU DPP, EPR and parcel rules, alongside stricter US forced-labour scrutiny, are turning compliance into a competitive advantage.
Exporters able to scale trusted data systems may gain stronger buyer confidence and sourcing preference.

title: Turkiye’s apparel export decline moderated in January-April 2026
summary:
Türkiye’s apparel exports declined 1.98 per cent year on year to $5.192 billion in January–April 2026 due to weak demand in Europe and rising competition from lower-cost Asian suppliers including Bangladesh, Vietnam and Pakistan.
However, exports rebounded sharply in April, rising 16.2 per cent on the back of seasonal orders and European restocking demand.

title: Decoding Indonesia’s evolving export strategy
summary:
Indonesia is gearing up to navigate mounting global uncertainties and reduce its reliance on select markets by pursuing export diversification, forging strategic trade partnerships, and deepening engagement with high-potential export destinations. 
The country is positioning strategic trade diplomacy alongside manufacturing strength as key to sustaining future export growth.

title: Evolving sourcing dynamics and the Vietnam-Bangladesh rivalry
summary:
While China continues to dominate global apparel exports, competition between Bangladesh and Vietnam is intensifying amid shifting sourcing trends. 
Bangladesh retains strength in low-cost, large-scale garment manufacturing, while Vietnam benefits from diversified products, faster logistics, stronger FTAs and quicker raw material access, strengthening its position in higher-value apparel exports.

title: Europe’s textile trade firewall moves beyond anti-dumping
summary:
Europe is expanding its textile and apparel trade defence beyond anti-dumping duties towards a broader compliance- and customs-driven shield against rising Chinese imports.
New parcel levies, traceability requirements and forced-labour enforcement are reshaping market access rules.
For suppliers, competitiveness in Europe will increasingly depend on compliance transparency.

title: Resale booms, but circular fashion economics still do not work
summary:
The resale and repair economy is pushing governments to reduce VAT, sales tax and labour costs on secondhand fashion.
Resale demand is rising strongly, but sorting, repair and sustainable material costs remain margin pressures.
With EPR rules expanding, circular fashion is shifting from a sustainability narrative towards a policy-driven industrial system.
